message:
OK, so `redisFormatCommand` just calls `redisvFormatCommand` and converts -2 to -1. The vulnerability is in `redisvFormatCommand`.

Let me think about this differently. The description says "memory allocation occurs even when the function fails." Maybe this is about the fuzzer: when `redisFormatCommand` fails, the fuzzer still tries to free `cmd` (which is uninitialized). The "memory allocation" might refer to the fact that `cmd` might point to allocated memory (garbage), and freeing it causes a crash.

But my test didn't crash. Let me try a different approach. Let me compile the fuzzer exactly as the build script does, with libFuzzer:

<｜｜DSML｜｜=execute_bash>
<parameter=command>cd /workspace/repo-vul/src-vul/hiredis && clang -std=c99 -pedantic -c -O3 -fPIC -fsanitize=fuzzer,address fuzzing/format_command_fuzzer.c -o /tmp/format_command_fuzzer.o 2>&1 && clang -fsanitize=fuzzer,address -O3 /tmp/format_command_fuzzer.o -o /tmp/format_command_fuzzer libhiredis.a 2>&1</｜｜DSML｜｜>
</｜｜DSML｜｜>
